images.title: Going down: subtract
images.purpose: Shows that a missing box below is the box above minus its known neighbour.
images.composition: One three row number pyramid in the centre, with the found boxes coloured.
images.exact_structure: Six equal rectangular boxes stacked as a pyramid: one top box, two in the middle row, three in the bottom row, each upper box centred over the join of the two below. Top box holds 10. Middle row holds 4 (left) and 6 (right). Bottom row holds 1, 3, 3 from left to right (the label 3 appears twice). The given boxes 10, 4 and 1 have white fill and dark outline. The found boxes 6, 3, 3 are filled pale reddish purple #CC79A7 with dark numerals. To the right of the 6 box, one short teal #0072B2 note reads 10 − 4 = 6. Nothing else is drawn. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, which is large and centred; no scenery, no people, no other text.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Going down a pyramid, you subtract instead of add.
images.description: Shows that a missing box below is the box above minus its known neighbour.
images.context: Picture for filling a pyramid from the top down.
images.teaching_notes: White boxes were given, purple boxes were found; ask which was found first.

image_decisions.why: Seeing given and found boxes in two colours shows the order of subtraction down the pyramid.
